verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding's conclusion is contradicted by the later messages in its own document, and its magnitude is invisible against this name's reaction distribution. The date confusion is real and published - docs/aa9cccc1...txt shows it running from 2026-08-12T18:20:41Z ('One site says the 20th, another says the 27th') through 2026-08-20 and 08-21. But the same file resolves it publicly on 2026-08-24T13:04:34Z: 'Fidelity was correct, the ER will be Sept 2.' That is nine calendar days and six sessions before the print, in the same feed, visible to the same participants. And crucially the file then shows the crowd re-positioning for the real date, not staying out: 2026-08-21T14:14:29Z 'bought some more for 2.825', 2026-08-21T13:39:36Z 'If you haven't bought for earnings run up, I think there's still time', 2026-08-28T14:57:07Z 'Earnings will be spectacular... It will then pop to 3, 4, per share', and 2026-08-28T13:57:31Z 'Exited all at $2.74 for tiny loss. Earnings in 2 days' - an exit taken with explicit knowledge of the correct date, which is ordinary pre-print risk management, not the residue of a two-week-old mistake. So the mechanism 'a lighter book arrives at the real print' is not established by the document it comes from; the document shows a crowd that learned the date and traded around it. Then the size check kills what is left. The hunter honestly says it is worth 'a fraction of a percent of conviction' on a $2.63 stock, and this name's baseline carries a 23.34% median reaction with an 11.67% deadband. A positioning nuance an order of magnitude below the deadband cannot rank against anything. Everything else in the finding is published sell-side material: the CFRA downgrade of 2026-08-19 and RBC's flat-sales, EBITDA-down-3% expectation are both in the captured feed, and they are what actually sets the bar. I hold the number at 68 rather than higher because the specific aggregation - that positioning was built for the wrong date - is genuinely written nowhere, and that is the one honest thing in the claim.

prior_publication.what_it_says: 'Fidelity was correct, the ER will be Sept 2' - the correct date was published in the same feed on 2026-08-24, six sessions before the print, so the confusion was resolved well pre-print.
The date confusion itself is published: competing 20th/26th/27th/Sept 3 dates and 'earnings after the close today' on 2026-08-20.
After the date was corrected, the same feed shows fresh buying 'for earnings run up' and a pre-print exit explicitly timed to 'Earnings in 2 days' - i.e. positioning was rebuilt around the real date.
A public 8-K with an item 7.01 press release - the company's own disclosures were on EDGAR through the run-in, whatever the retail feed noticed.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The bars show what the finding describes but not what it concludes: the stock reached about 2.95 around 2026-08-19/20 on the mistaken expectation and closed at 2.63 into the print, run_up_5d -5.05% and run_up_20d -9.93% on a 1,697,640-share average. That unwind is in the price. The decisive baseline fact is scale: seven prints, 23.34% median absolute reaction, 34.58% maximum, and an 11.67% deadband. A claim its own author sizes at a fraction of a percent is roughly two orders of magnitude below the move this print will produce, so even if wholly unpriced it cannot separate this name from any other. Baseline is sound (fits_cadence, 7 events, no session conflicts).
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Open-interest or share-lending data showing positioning was materially lighter into 2026-09-02 than into comparable prints - the measurement the claim asserts but never makes - together with a size that is at least a meaningful fraction of the 11.67% deadband.
verdicts.note_on_the_independence_claim: The hunter argues that the retail stream's failure to mention three item 5.02 8-Ks 'independently establishes that the capture's coverage is not tracking the company's disclosures'. I accept that as a statement about the capture, and it is a fair and unusually candid one - but it cuts against the finding rather than for it, because it concedes the corpus is not a reliable proxy for what the market saw.

interactions: The claim, its counter-evidence and the sell-side bar (CFRA 2026-08-19, RBC) all live in one document, docs/aa9cccc1...txt; the filings-based 'independence' note is about the same corpus's blind spots rather than about the market.
corpus_limits: WOOF's capture has 69 items and no news documents, so I cannot see the company's own earnings-date press release, any wire confirmation of the date, or the RBC and CFRA notes in full - only their relay in the retail feed. There is no options chain and no open-interest series, so the central positioning assertion is not measurable in either direction from this corpus. I have not treated the retail feed's confusion as evidence about institutional positioning.
